newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges Congress to pass budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges Congress to pass budget plan.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Saturday urged rank-and-file members of Congress to approve a balanced budget plan hammered out in weeks of negotiations with leaders of the Republican-led Congress.

"Let us now reach across party lines and seize our chance to balance the budget," he said in his weekly radio address a day after the budget agreement was made to balance the budget by 2002 and cut some taxes.

The plan appears to have strong support from members of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Final disputes over tax cuts and Clinton's spending initiatives were essentially swept aside on Thursday night when the Congressional Budget Office came out with a new economic forecast that predicted the government would bring in $225 billion more revenue over five years than previous projections.

Answering questions from reporters after delivering his radio address, Clinton said the new projections helped seal the agreement but that budget negotiators only forecast spending a small portion of the $225 billion, leaving the rest for deficit reduction.
He said if the projections proved accurate, the budget could come into balance even before 2002. "I urge members of Congress in both parties to pass it," Clinton said.
